newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Rank looks to fast pub roll out.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Rank looks to fast pub roll out.

text.p: The Rank Organisation Plc expects a fast underlying profit stream from its purchase of Tom Cobleigh public houses as it aims to open new pubs swiftly, chief executive Andrew Teare told Reuters in an interview.
"There is an underlying velocity in the profit streams," he said, adding that around 16 new pubs should be opened this year and next year. Rank wanted to open "at least that and maybe a few more".
Rank said earlier on Tuesday it had agreed to pay 240 pence a share to buy Tom Cobleigh, valuing the public house chain at around 95.6 million stg.
It said in a statement the deal should have a neutral impact on earnings in the first full financial year and be earnings enhancing after that.
Tom Cobleigh's managing director Derek Mapp added that the company had planned on its own to open 22 new outlets next year but under Rank's ownership this could be speeded up.
Rank's move "guarantees growth (for Tom Cobleigh) and gives opportunities to roll out our development programme", he said.
Teare said Rank would also benefit from synergies between the two companies, particulary in purchases of spirits and other alcoholic drinks, where Rank is one of the UK's largest players.
He said the deal would give Rank the chance to offer eating out facilities in its leisure complexes. "The one thing we don't have is an eating-out business."
Rank's leisure and entertainment complexes currently rely on leasing out space to restaurant chains but the Tom Cobleigh purchase means it can run its own food outlets, Teare said.
"We can make substantial inroads to capture those eating out revenues," he said. "It is a big add-on to our existing strategy," he said.
Mapp said Tom Cobleigh could achieve its aim of becoming a national brand with Rank. He suggested this meant having over 100 outlets.
By the end of this year, Tom Cobleigh should have 54 outlets, he added.
